## Container plumbing

Per-app Podman state directories, port binding and runtime identity (`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`).

### `myContainerApp`

Containerized apps' shared plumbing: per-app state dirs, the
127.0.0.1 host-port bind, runtime user identity, and TZ. Mirrors
`myCaddy.apps` — one declaration per app, emitted into
`systemd.tmpfiles.rules` and `virtualisation.oci-containers.containers`.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.capabilities`

Capability names without `CAP_`. When set, the container
runs with `--cap-drop=ALL` plus one `--cap-add` for each
entry; null keeps podman's default set. An image whose
root init signals an app running as another uid (e.g.
tini forwarding SIGTERM after su-exec) needs `KILL`, or
`podman stop` cannot reach the app.

- **Type:** `null or (list of string matching the pattern [A-Z_]+)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "CHOWN"
    "KILL"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.cleanStopExitStatus`

Exit statuses, besides 0, that the container's unit
treats as a clean stop (`SuccessExitStatus`). Set 143
when the app exits by re-raising the SIGTERM it was
stopped with; otherwise a clean `systemctl stop` leaves
the unit failed, which aborts a recovery restore.

- **Type:** `list of 8 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 255 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    143
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.containerPort`

Port the app listens on inside the container. Defaults to `port`.

- **Type:** `null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `config.port`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.linuxServer`

Emit PUID/PGID env (server uid/gid) instead of a container
`user =` override, for images that start as root and drop
privileges themselves (linuxserver.io-style entrypoints).
Only meaningful when `manageUser` is true.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.manageUser`

Whether this module sets the container's runtime user identity.
Set false for images that take their uid/gid via app-specific env
vars the module doesn't model (e.g. grimmory's USER_ID/GROUP_ID) —
the app module then sets those itself.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.port`

Host port to publish on 127.0.0.1. Left null for apps that
don't publish a host port at all (e.g. valheim, which uses
`--network=host` and opens UDP game ports on the firewall
directly) — no `ports` entry is emitted in that case.

- **Type:** `null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.stateDirGroup`

Group for the stateDirs tmpfiles rules. Defaults to the servers gid.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `toString serverGid`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.stateDirOwner`

Owner for the stateDirs tmpfiles rules. Defaults to the server user's uid.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `toString serverUid`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.stateDirs`

Host directories to create (0750, owned by stateDirOwner:stateDirGroup)
for this container's persistent state. Multi-subdir apps list every
subdir they bind-mount.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ "/var/lib/containers/${name}" ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myContainerApp.<name>.tzEnv`

Emit `TZ = config.time.timeZone` in the container environment.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

### `myPodmanPrune.keepImages`

Extra image references the prune must never remove, for images
run outside `virtualisation.oci-containers` — a timer-driven
`podman run --rm` oneshot has no container object between runs,
so it is invisible to any liveness-based prune, and a
nix-built image carries a SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 manifest
timestamp, so the age window matches it too. The
oci-containers list is collected automatically; this is only
for out-of-band callers. Declare it next to the `podman run`
that uses the image so the ref and its renovate annotation stay
in one place.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "ghcr.io/ianepreston/spierscraper:2026.07.17.1"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/oci-containers.nix`](../../modules/system/oci-containers.nix)

## Service endpoints

The published URL + readiness-unit contract cross-module consumers use instead of reading another module's `services.*`.

### `myServiceEndpoints`

Locally consumable service endpoints. A producing module declares a
URL and its readiness unit; a consuming module uses that contract
instead of reading the producer's implementation configuration.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/service-endpoints.nix`](../../modules/system/service-endpoints.nix)

### `myServiceEndpoints.<name>.containerUrl`

URL a container on the default podman bridge uses to reach
the ‹name› service, normally via
`host.containers.internal`. Set only by a producer that
listens on the bridge; null means containers cannot reach
it. Never a loopback or wildcard address: an assertion
rejects every literal spelling of one, as well as
userinfo and any whitespace or control character. That a host name
resolves to this host from inside a container is the
producer's responsibility.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Example:** `"http://host.containers.internal:8080"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/service-endpoints.nix`](../../modules/system/service-endpoints.nix)

### `myServiceEndpoints.<name>.unit`

Systemd unit local consumers order after before reaching ‹name›.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Example:** `"example.service"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/service-endpoints.nix`](../../modules/system/service-endpoints.nix)

### `myServiceEndpoints.<name>.url`

URL local host processes use to reach the ‹name› service.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/service-endpoints.nix`](../../modules/system/service-endpoints.nix)

## State, backup and recovery

One declaration per piece of state, rendered into preservation, restic paths, SQLite staging and the recovery manifest; see [app-state.md](../agents/app-state.md) and the [backup runbook](../runbooks/backup-restore.md).

### `myAppState`

Server-owned on-disk state. Keyed by owner name; each entry is
the single source of truth for that owner's persisted state
directory, deriving the impermanence preservation entry and,
by default, the restic backup path.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.backup`

Whether to include this state in the server's restic
backup. Set false for data that must survive a reboot but
is intentionally not restorable, such as incomplete
downloads, derived metrics, or re-downloadable caches.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.backupPath`

Path to back up with restic. Null (the default) backs
up `stateDir`; override only when the backup source
differs from the preserved directory.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.dynamicUser`

The owning service uses systemd `DynamicUser=` with a
`StateDirectory=` under /var/lib/private. systemd keeps
such a directory on disk as nobody:nogroup, with the
unit's `StateDirectoryMode=` (default 0755), and id-maps
it to the service's transient UID at start, so the
preservation entry must assert that same owner and
mode. Leaving the preservation default (root) in place
means every `systemd-tmpfiles-resetup` run on a switch
hands the top-level directory back to root under the
running service, which then cannot write to it (or,
at 0700, even traverse it) until restarted (#949).

Setting this changes the `user`/`group` defaults to
nobody/nogroup (overriding either is an eval error)
and the `mode` default to 0755. Set `mode` to match
the unit's `StateDirectoryMode=` when upstream
changes it, or the two fight over the mode instead.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.group`

Group of the preserved directory. Defaults to the
shared `servers` group used by NFS-aligned apps; set to
the app's own group for apps that run as a per-package
user, or null to omit (root).

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `if dynamicUser then "nogroup" else "servers"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.mode`

Mode of the preserved directory.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `if dynamicUser then "0755" else "0700"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.stateDir`

The app's persisted state directory (e.g.
"/var/lib/radarr"). For DynamicUser services whose
real storage lives under /var/lib/private/&lt;app&gt;, use
that private path — it is what actually needs
preserving and backing up.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppState.<name>.user`

Owner of the preserved directory. Null omits the field
from the preservation entry, so preservation's default
(root) applies. Not suitable for DynamicUser services:
preservation renders that default into a tmpfiles `d`
rule, which re-asserts it on an existing directory. Use
`dynamicUser` for those.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `if dynamicUser then "nobody" else null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppStateAudit.exemptions`

Owner-local exemptions from the `StateDirectory=` coverage audit,
keyed by owner name and declared beside the service they cover.
The audit runs on every host with preservation enabled; a unit's
state directory that no preserved directory covers fails eval
unless an entry here names that unit and directory.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppStateAudit.exemptions.<name>.directories`

Normalized absolute state directories of `unit`, as the
audit names them: /var/lib/&lt;dir&gt;, or
/var/lib/private/&lt;dir&gt; for a DynamicUser unit.

- **Type:** `non-empty (list of string)`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "/var/lib/private/homepage-dashboard"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppStateAudit.exemptions.<name>.disposition`

`disposable`: the owner decided the state may be lost on
every reboot. `pending`: a known uncovered directory
still awaiting the owner's preserve-or-discard decision;
it passes eval but emits a warning on every build.

- **Type:** `one of "disposable", "pending"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppStateAudit.exemptions.<name>.reason`

Why the state may be lost, or what decision is pending. Must not be empty.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myAppStateAudit.exemptions.<name>.unit`

The systemd unit, with its `.service` suffix.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Example:** `"homepage-dashboard.service"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/app-state.nix`](../../modules/system/app-state.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps`

Recovery metadata contributed by server-app modules. `task
recovery:app APP=&lt;name&gt;` evaluates the generated manifest and
passes these values to the existing restore templates.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.database`

Postgres database replayed by the postgres template.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.health`

Optional loopback HTTP health probe after restoration.

- **Type:** `null or (submodule)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.health.expect`

_No description._

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"200"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.health.retries`

_No description._

- **Type:** `signed integer`
- **Default:** `30`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.health.sleep`

_No description._

- **Type:** `signed integer`
- **Default:** `2`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.health.url`

_No description._

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.kind`

Existing recovery template this app uses.

- **Type:** `one of "volume", "postgres", "sqlite"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.order`

Explicit catastrophic-restore ordering. Leave gaps between
values so a new dependency can be inserted without
renumbering unrelated apps.

- **Type:** `signed integer`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.paths`

Non-Postgres paths restored with the app.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.sqliteOwner`

Owner passed to the SQLite swap template. The default is
the target host's server-environment user; services with
their own static user override it.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"@env@"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.apps.<name>.units`

Systemd units stopped and started around the restore.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `myRecovery.manifest`

Machine-readable recovery metadata generated from `apps` and the
existing SQLite-quiesce declarations. It contains no secrets and
is intended for `nix eval --json` by taskfiles/recovery.yaml.

- **Type:** `attribute set of anything`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/recovery.nix`](../../modules/system/recovery.nix)

### `mySqliteQuiesce.apps`

Apps with SQLite databases that should be quiesced before
restic-backups-server fires. Each entry lists absolute paths
to .db files; the helper creates one oneshot per app that
runs `sqlite3 .backup` for each into
/var/backup/sqlite/&lt;name&gt;/&lt;basename&gt; and orders it before
the nightly restic snapshot.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/sqlite-quiesce.nix`](../../modules/system/sqlite-quiesce.nix)

### `mySqliteQuiesce.apps.<name>.databases`

Absolute paths to SQLite files. The basename ends up
in /var/backup/sqlite/&lt;name&gt;/&lt;basename&gt;, so basenames
must be distinct within an app: no two entries may share
a staged file. A collision between names known at
evaluation fails evaluation. Staged names may only use
letters, digits and `._+@%,:=~-`, because sqlite's
`.backup` takes them unquoted; a literal path with any
other basename fails evaluation.
An entry may be a glob for a path the app picks at
runtime (wealthfolio's per-profile directory); it must
match exactly one file, and the quiesce unit fails
otherwise. Recovery resolves the same glob on restore.
When a glob's last component is anything but a plain
safe name (a pattern, a shell escape such as
`plain\.db`), its staged name is checked once resolved:
the unit fails before writing any staged copy if two
entries would share one or a resolved name has any
other character. A hidden file only matches a pattern
that spells out its leading dot (`.*.db`).

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/sqlite-quiesce.nix`](../../modules/system/sqlite-quiesce.nix)

## Credentials and databases

App-generated API keys read at boot, and Postgres roles with sops-managed passwords.

### `myPostgresApp`

Apps that consume the shared native postgres instance with a
sops-managed password. The helper provisions the db + role +
rotation oneshot; the app module is responsible for plumbing
the password into its own env file and pointing the upstream
service at host.containers.internal:5432.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/postgresql.nix`](../../modules/system/postgresql.nix)

### `myPostgresApp.<name>.consumerService`

Systemd units that consume this role and must wait
for the password rotation oneshot to complete. The
oneshot is wired with `before` and `wantedBy` on
every listed unit, so no consumer ever starts with
a stale password. Pass every unit that opens a
connection (e.g. paperless-ngx with
paperless-{web,scheduler,task-queue,consumer})
rather than trusting transitive ordering through a
single representative unit.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/postgresql.nix`](../../modules/system/postgresql.nix)

### `myPostgresApp.<name>.dbName`

Postgres database (and role) name. Defaults to the
attribute name with hyphens replaced by underscores
(paperless-ngx → paperless_ngx) so the role name is
a valid SQL identifier.

Must be a plain identifier (letters, digits, `_`
and `$`), since the password rotation passes it to
`ALTER USER` unquoted. Each app owns its database
and role exclusively, compared as PostgreSQL
resolves the name: folded to lower case and
truncated to 63 bytes. Two entries resolving to one
name (`foo-bar` and `foo_bar`, `Foo` and `foo`, or
two names sharing their first 63 bytes) fail
evaluation. No app shares one. Known limits: the
reserved role names `current_user` and `session_user`,
and names containing `$`, are not rejected; don't
use them.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/postgresql.nix`](../../modules/system/postgresql.nix)

### `myPostgresApp.<name>.secretName`

sops secret name for the role's password. Defaults
to "&lt;name&gt;/db_password". Override only if the
secret already exists under a non-standard name.
Must be unique across entries: a shared secret would
restart only one app's rotation oneshot, so a
collision fails evaluation.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›/db_password"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/postgresql.nix`](../../modules/system/postgresql.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.consumers`

Services that need credentials at runtime. Each entry emits
a `<name>-credentials.service` oneshot rendering the
requested readers into `envFile`, which the consuming units
read via `EnvironmentFile=` (or podman's `--env-file`).

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.consumers.<name>.envFile`

Path of the rendered env file. Read-only; reference it from the consuming service.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"/run/‹name›-credentials/env"`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.consumers.<name>.envVarPrefix`

Prepended to each reader name in the rendered file.
Homepage needs `HOMEPAGE_VAR_` on anything it
substitutes into widget config; most consumers
read the bare name and leave this empty.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `""`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.consumers.<name>.units`

Units that consume `envFile`. Ordered after the
oneshot, and restarted by it whenever it runs —
an env-file change doesn't bust a unit's drv hash,
so a plain `nixos-rebuild switch` wouldn't
otherwise pick up a rotated key.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.consumers.<name>.vars`

Reader names to render into this consumer's env
file. Every entry must exist in `readers` — an
assertion catches typos at eval time.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.readerPath`

Tools every `readScript` may rely on. Any unit that runs a
reader puts these on its PATH (`systemd.services.<unit>.path`).

- **Type:** `list of package`
- **Default:** `with pkgs; [ coreutils gnugrep gnused gawk jq sqlite ]`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.readers`

Registry of readable credentials, keyed by the env var name
consumers will see (e.g. `PROWLARR_API_KEY`). Declared by
the app module that owns the generating service; consuming
it is a separate opt-in via `consumers.<name>.vars`.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.readers.<name>.readScript`

Shell snippet that prints the credential value to
stdout (no trailing newline). Runs as root with
`readerPath` on PATH. Empty/missing output is tolerated by
`consumers` — the env line is omitted rather than
blocking the consumer; a unit running the script
directly applies its own policy.

- **Type:** `strings concatenated with "\n"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

### `myRuntimeCredentials.readers.<name>.sourceUnit`

Systemd unit that produces the config file or DB the
reader pulls from. Pulled into After=/Wants= on every
consumer that reads this credential, so the upstream
service has started (and on first boot, has written
its config) before we try to read it.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix`](../../modules/system/runtime-credentials.nix)

## Single sign-on

OIDC and forward-auth registrations hosted beside the IDP; see the [Authentik runbook](../runbooks/authentik-sso.md) and [authentik.md](../agents/authentik.md).

### `myAuthentik.extraBlueprints`

Extra blueprint directories or files to merge into authentik's
blueprints_dir alongside the bundled defaults. Each entry is a
path containing one or more *.yaml blueprint files. Other app
modules can append their own blueprints here so each app stays
self-contained.

- **Type:** `list of absolute path`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps`

Apps gated by authentik forward-auth via Caddy. Each entry
generates an authentik proxy provider + application + policy
binding (default group: Infrastructure), plus a Caddy route
and (optionally) a homepage tile. One blueprint owns the
embedded outpost's `providers` list, so every forward-auth
app on the host must register through this option rather than
emitting its own outpost block.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.authentikGroup`

Authentik group whose members can access this app via
the policy binding. Defaults to Infrastructure (admin
tools); set to Users for end-user-facing apps.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"Infrastructure"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.bypassAuthPaths`

Caddy `path` patterns that skip forward_auth and reach
the upstream directly. Use for apps that ship their
own API-key auth on a sub-path (sonarr/radarr at
/api/*, RSS calendars at /feed/*) so non-browser
clients can authenticate with the app's native scheme
instead of getting redirected to the authentik login
flow. Empty (default) gates every path through
authentik. Patterns follow Caddy `path` matcher
semantics: `/foo/*` is a prefix match on `/foo/`,
anything without a trailing `*` is an exact match.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "/api/*"
    "/ping"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.displayName`

Human-facing app name (authentik tile + homepage label).

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.homepage`

Homepage tile metadata. Set to null (default) to
skip generating a tile. When set, `group` is
required so the tile lands in the right section
instead of defaulting to a catch-all.

- **Type:** `null or (submodule)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.homepage.description`

Short blurb shown beneath the app on the homepage tile.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.homepage.group`

Homepage layout group this app appears under. Required:
no implicit default — set this per app so tiles land in
the right group instead of all defaulting to one place.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.homepage.icon`

homepage icon slug (resolves against dashboard-icons).

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.homepage.widget`

Optional homepage widget block. Passed through to the
generated tile via `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.widget`. See
https://gethomepage.dev/widgets/ for per-type fields.

- **Type:** `null or (attribute set of unspecified value)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.host`

External hostname Caddy matches and authentik enforces.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"<name>.${hostSpec.serverDomain}"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.iconUrl`

Icon URL used on the authentik application tile.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/homarr-labs/dashboard-icons/main/png/‹name›.png"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.port`

Port the upstream exposes on `upstreamHost`. Set this
for a proxied app; it is mutually exclusive with
`staticRouteConfig`.

- **Type:** `null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.proxyConfig`

Extra directives spliced into the caddy `reverse_proxy`
body. Use this to inject `header_up` lines for apps
that consume authentik headers (translating an
X-authentik-* header into the Remote-* name an app
expects), or transport directives like omada's.

- **Type:** `strings concatenated with "\n"`
- **Default:** `""`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.staticRouteConfig`

Caddy directives serving a static app after
forward-auth. Set this instead of `port` for an app
whose entire response is Caddy-served files rather than
a local HTTP upstream. The generated Authentik provider,
application, policy binding, and homepage tile remain
identical to proxied apps.

- **Type:** `null or strings concatenated with "\n"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.upstreamBearerEnvVar`

Name of an environment variable in caddy's
EnvironmentFile holding a bearer token for the
upstream. When set, two things change:

* `bypassAuthPaths` additionally require an
  `Authorization` header to be present, so the
  bypass only applies to genuine API clients; and
* the authentik-gated branch injects
  `Authorization: Bearer $${env.<VAR>}` upstream.

Use it for an upstream that enforces its own bearer
auth on every route, where the browser would
otherwise be prompted for a shared key it has
already earned by logging into authentik. It also
tightens the bypass: an unauthenticated request to
a bypassed path lands on authentik instead of
reaching the upstream at all.

The app module is responsible for stacking the
env file onto caddy, as the app module that front-ends the
upstream does.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Example:** `"LLAMA_API_KEY"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.forwardAuthApps.<name>.upstreamHost`

Host Caddy proxies to. Defaults to localhost — nearly
every app runs on the same box as caddy. Set it to
front a service on *another* machine that has no
caddy/authentik of its own (for example a workstation's
llama-server),
so that machine gets TLS + SSO without replicating
the whole server stack. The hop is plaintext HTTP
over the LAN, so only point this at a backend with
its own auth on the paths you bypass.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"localhost"`
- **Example:** `"workstation.example.internal"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.ldap.enable`

Whether to enable authentik's LDAP outpost. Renders the LDAP provider /
application / ldapservice user blueprint, wires the
worker-side bind password, and starts `services.authentik-
ldap` against a sops-templated env file. Used by apps
(jellyfin) that can only authenticate against authentik
via LDAP — TV/native clients don't do OIDC redirects, so
same-credentials login is the goal, not full SSO.

One-time manual setup is required to capture the outpost
token: see docs/runbooks/jellyfin.md.
.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps`

Apps that authenticate against Authentik via OIDC directly
(the app speaks OIDC; we do not use the embedded outpost).
Each entry generates the sops secret pair, contributes a
blueprint dir, and stacks a single merged worker env file
onto Authentik so blueprint `!Env` placeholders resolve.

Apps that read OIDC creds from env vars also get a per-app
env file the upstream image consumes. Apps that read OIDC
creds from their own database (audiobookshelf, kavita,
seerr) opt out by setting `clientCredsInAppEnv = false`.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.appRestartUnit`

Systemd units to restart when the per-app env
file changes. Required (non-empty) when
`clientCredsInAppEnv` is true or `extraEnvLines`
is non-empty. Leave as the empty default for
apps with no per-app env file (e.g.
audiobookshelf, kavita, seerr — all DB/UI
configured). Pass every unit that consumes the
env file (e.g. paperless-ngx with
paperless-{web,scheduler,consumer,task-queue})
so they all bounce on credential rotation.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.blueprintsDir`

Path to a directory of *.yaml blueprint files for
this app. The dir is contributed via
`myAuthentik.extraBlueprints` and merged into
authentik's blueprints_dir.

- **Type:** `absolute path`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.clientCredsInAppEnv`

Whether the per-app env file should include the
OIDC client_id (and client_secret unless
`publicClient`). Set to false when the app reads
these from its own database/UI rather than env.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.clientIdVar`

Env var name the upstream image reads for the OIDC client id.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"OIDC_CLIENT_ID"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.clientSecretVar`

Env var name the upstream image reads for the OIDC client secret.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.displayName`

Human-facing app name (authentik tile + homepage
label). Defaults to the attribute name.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.envFileName`

Name of the sops template the per-app env file is
registered under. Reference it in the upstream
service via `config.sops.templates."<name>".path`.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›.env"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.extraEnvLines`

Extra `KEY=value` lines appended to the per-app
env file. Use this for db passwords, secret keys,
or inline-JSON env vars whose values come from
other sops placeholders. Whatever placeholders
this string references must be declared via
`extraSecrets`.

- **Type:** `strings concatenated with "\n"`
- **Default:** `""`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.extraSecrets`

Additional sops secret declarations merged into
sops.secrets. Use this for db passwords, signing
keys, etc. that the per-app env file references
via `extraEnvLines`.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (attribute set)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.homepage`

Homepage tile metadata. Set to null (default) to
skip generating a tile.

- **Type:** `null or (submodule)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.homepage.description`

Short blurb shown beneath the app on the homepage tile.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.homepage.group`

Homepage layout group this app appears under. Required:
no implicit default — set this per app so tiles land in
the right group instead of all defaulting to one place.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.homepage.icon`

homepage icon slug (resolves against dashboard-icons).

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.homepage.widget`

Optional homepage widget block. Passed through to the
generated tile via `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.widget`. See
https://gethomepage.dev/widgets/ for per-type fields.

- **Type:** `null or (attribute set of unspecified value)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.publicClient`

True for OIDC public clients (PKCE, no
client_secret). When true, only oidc_client_id
is provisioned; client_secret is omitted from
both sops and the env files.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

### `myAuthentik.oidcApps.<name>.startupProbeUnits`

Units that probe the OIDC discovery URL at startup but
are not restarted by the per-app env file (e.g. bindery,
which keeps its OIDC config in its own database and
latches a failed discovery). They are ordered after
this app's blueprint-applied gate exactly like
`appRestartUnit`, without being restart targets.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/authentik.nix`](../../modules/apps/authentik.nix)

## Routing and dashboard

Reverse-proxy routes on the wildcard vhost and homepage tiles.

### `myCaddy.apps`

Apps routed via the wildcard `*.${hostSpec.serverDomain}` virtualHost.
One wildcard cert covers every entry here, so adding apps doesn't
consume Let's Encrypt rate-limit budget.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/caddy.nix`](../../modules/system/caddy.nix)

### `myCaddy.apps.<name>.host`

Hostnames matched for this app, whitespace-separated.
Defaults to &lt;name&gt;.&lt;serverDomain&gt;.

One owner per host: no request host may be matched by
two apps, since only one of their routes could ever be
served. Hosts are compared as Caddy matches them
(case-insensitively, a whole-label `*` matching any
one label), so `*.lab.<serverDomain>` and
`x.lab.<serverDomain>` in different apps fail
evaluation, as do a quoted and a bare spelling of one
name; a trailing dot is treated as the same name.
Write plain ASCII hostnames (Punycode for
internationalized names) with no port, placeholder or
partial-label wildcard: those cannot be compared and
fail evaluation. No intentional sharing is supported.
Known limit: a hostname containing a carriage return or
another control character is not detected as a
duplicate; don't write one.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"<name>.${hostSpec.serverDomain}"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/caddy.nix`](../../modules/system/caddy.nix)

### `myCaddy.apps.<name>.routeConfig`

Caddy directives for this app's `handle` block. Typically a
single `reverse_proxy` directive, with `import authentik_forward_auth`
prepended for apps that don't speak OIDC themselves.

- **Type:** `strings concatenated with "\n"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/caddy.nix`](../../modules/system/caddy.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles`

Flat per-tile attrset. Each entry becomes one tile under the
named `group`. Sort within a group is by `weight` (low to
high), then alphabetical by `displayName`. Group display
order is controlled by services.homepage-dashboard.settings.layout
below.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.description`

Short blurb shown beneath the tile label.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.displayName`

Label shown on the tile. Defaults to the attribute name.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.group`

Layout group this tile appears under (e.g.
"Consumption", "Acquisition", "Infrastructure").
Required: no implicit default.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.href`

URL the tile links to.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.icon`

Icon — either a dashboard-icons slug (e.g. `sonarr`)
or a full URL to an image.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.weight`

Sort weight within the group. Lower values render
first. Ties break alphabetically by displayName.

- **Type:** `signed integer`
- **Default:** `0`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

### `myHomepage.tiles.<name>.widget`

Optional homepage widget block emitted on this tile.
The attrset is passed through to the rendered
services.yaml verbatim; required keys (e.g. `type`,
`url`, `key`) depend on the widget type. Reference
credentials via `{{HOMEPAGE_VAR_<NAME>}}` and register
the matching reader under `myRuntimeCredentials.readers`.
See https://gethomepage.dev/widgets/.

- **Type:** `null or (attribute set of unspecified value)`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/homepage.nix`](../../modules/system/homepage.nix)

## Observability

Alert rules, monitored units and exporter drop directories that apps contribute to the platform.

### `myObservability.logRuleGroups`

Application-owned VictoriaLogs rule groups, keyed by the
contributing module. The platform combines these with its generic
security and configuration-change groups.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/observability-options.nix`](../../modules/system/observability-options.nix)

### `myObservability.logRuleGroups.<name>.groups`

VictoriaLogs/vmalert rule groups contributed by one application.

- **Type:** `list of (attribute set)`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/observability-options.nix`](../../modules/system/observability-options.nix)

### `myObservability.metricRuleGroups`

Application-owned VictoriaMetrics rule groups, keyed by the
contributing module. The platform combines these with its host,
hardware, power, and security groups when configuring vmalert.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/observability-options.nix`](../../modules/system/observability-options.nix)

### `myObservability.metricRuleGroups.<name>.groups`

VictoriaMetrics/vmalert rule groups contributed by one application.

- **Type:** `list of (attribute set)`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/observability-options.nix`](../../modules/system/observability-options.nix)

### `myObservability.monitoredSystemdUnits`

systemd-unit regular-expression alternatives to include in the
node_exporter systemd collector. App modules contribute the units
whose failure and restart behaviour they own; this stack owns the
collector and generic alerts that consume the resulting metrics.
Entries omit the common `.service` suffix.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "podman-example"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/observability-options.nix`](../../modules/system/observability-options.nix)

### `myObservability.nodeExporterTextfileDirectory`

The single node_exporter textfile-collector drop directory. Every
producer that publishes `*.prom` files reads this, and
victoriametrics.nix (which owns the directory's creation and the
node_exporter `--collector.textfile.directory` flag) reads it too,
so a move needs to change one value rather than nine hand-synced
literals. Read-only: this is a shared contract, not a per-host knob.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"/var/lib/node-exporter-textfile-collector"`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/observability-options.nix`](../../modules/system/observability-options.nix)

## Local LLM inference

The llama.cpp router a host serves and the metrics endpoints a host publishes for routers; procedures are in the [local LLM runbook](../runbooks/local-llm.md).

### `myLlamaCpp.allowedClients`

Source addresses (iptables `-s` syntax — a bare IPv4 address
or a CIDR) allowed to reach `port`. Empty (the default) opens
nothing, which is correct for a loopback-only bind. Prefer
listing the single reverse-proxy host over a whole subnet: the
hop is plaintext HTTP and llama-server's own `--api-key` is
the only thing in front of it.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "192.0.2.11"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.cudaCapabilities`

CUDA compute capabilities to compile kernels for — exactly the
host's GPU, nothing else. RTX 5080 (Blackwell) is "12.0",
RTX 3070 (Ampere) is "8.6". Getting this wrong doesn't fail
the build; it fails at runtime with no usable kernels.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "12.0"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.enable`

Whether to enable llama.cpp's on-demand model router.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.evalTargets`

Read-only evaluation-facing export for local tooling. Combines the
declared role/budget with the active model's sizing assumptions.

- **Type:** `attribute set`
- **Default:** _computed from other options; see the declaration_
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.evaluation.residentBudgetMiB`

GPU memory available to a candidate after this host's desktop
or NVENC workload has taken its share. This is an evaluation
budget, not nominal card capacity.

- **Type:** `positive integer, meaning >0`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.evaluation.targets`

Alias-level evaluation roles. The radar derives active context,
KV types and offload settings, then consumes only evalTargets.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.evaluation.targets.<name>.modalities`

Input modalities a candidate must support for this alias.

- **Type:** `list of (one of "text", "image")`
- **Default:**

  ```nix
  [
    "text"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.evaluation.targets.<name>.role`

The job this alias is evaluated to replace.

- **Type:** `one of "generalist", "coding", "vision"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.extraFlags`

Additional llama-server flags appended after the ones this
module builds.

Service-wide only. llama.cpp merges the router's argv into
every child at the *highest* precedence, above both the
per-model preset section and the preset's global section — so
a model-shaped flag here (`-c`, `-ngl`, `-ctk`) silently wins
over every `models.<name>` entry. Put those in `models`.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "--flash-attn"
    "on"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.listenAddress`

Bind address. Leave at loopback when a reverse proxy on the
same host fronts the service. NixOS may widen it in combination
with `allowedClients`, which decides who can reach the port.
Darwin requires 127.0.0.1.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"127.0.0.1"`
- **Example:** `"0.0.0.0"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models`

The models this host's router serves, keyed by the
`<hf-repo>:<quant-tag>` string llama-server uses as both the
`-hf` argument and the model's routing name.

The key has to be exactly that string. The router derives the
same name independently when it scans `LLAMA_CACHE`, and the
two are merged by name — a key in any other shape produces a
*second*, unconfigured entry alongside the cached one, and a
client can reach it with llama.cpp's defaults instead of the
sizing below.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  {
    "Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M" = {
      aliases = [ "vision" ];
      ctxSize = 98304;
    };
  }
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models.<name>.aliases`

Extra names this model answers to, in addition to its
`<repo>:<tag>` key. Point clients at a role name here
rather than the GGUF's name, so swapping the model
underneath is a change to this file and not to every
client. Must not collide with another model's key or
aliases; llama-server refuses to start if they do.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "vision"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models.<name>.cacheTypeK`

KV cache data type for keys (`-ctk`). Quantizing the
cache is what buys context on a card the model has
already mostly filled: `q8_0` halves the per-token KV
cost for a few percent of generation throughput and a
quality hit far smaller than quantizing weights
further. Set both this and `cacheTypeV` — llama.cpp
takes them separately and there is no reason to split
them here.

- **Type:** `one of "f32", "f16", "bf16", "q8_0", "q5_0", "q5_1", "q4_0", "q4_1", "iq4_nl"`
- **Default:** `"f16"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models.<name>.cacheTypeV`

KV cache data type for values (`-ctv`). See `cacheTypeK`.

- **Type:** `one of "f32", "f16", "bf16", "q8_0", "q5_0", "q5_1", "q4_0", "q4_1", "iq4_nl"`
- **Default:** `"f16"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models.<name>.ctxSize`

Context window in tokens (`-c`). Sized per model *and*
per host: the KV cache for this context has to fit in
whatever VRAM the model weights leave behind. Only one
model is resident at a time (`--models-max 1`), so
each is budgeted against the whole card, not a share.

- **Type:** `positive integer, meaning >0`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Example:** `32768`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models.<name>.nCpuMoeLayers`

For a mixture-of-experts model, how many of its layers
keep their *expert* weights in system RAM (`-ncmoe`).
Zero (the default) is "none", which is the only
correct value for a dense model — it has no experts to
move.

This is a different lever from `nGpuLayers` and they
compose: `-ngl 99 -ncmoe N` keeps attention and the KV
cache for every layer on the GPU while the first N
layers' expert FFN weights live in host RAM. That
split is what makes a model whose weights exceed the
card usable at all — an MoE activates a small
fraction of its parameters per token, so the traffic
over PCIe is far smaller than the resident size
suggests, whereas moving whole layers with `-ngl`
would drag the KV cache off the card with them.

Cost is paid twice: throughput drops monotonically as
N rises, and the offloaded weights occupy host RAM for
as long as the model is loaded (~14 GB for
Qwen3-Coder-30B at N=40; the local LLM runbook has the
sizing numbers). That second cost is gentler than it looks — the
experts are an mmap of the GGUF, so almost all of it
is reclaimable page cache rather than committed
memory — but the throughput above assumes it stays
resident, and `sleepIdleSeconds` hands back VRAM, not
this.

- **Type:** `unsigned integer, meaning >=0`
- **Default:** `0`
- **Example:** `40`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.models.<name>.nGpuLayers`

Layers offloaded to the GPU (`-ngl`). The default is
the "everything" idiom — any value at or above the
model's layer count offloads the whole model. Lower it
only to deliberately keep layers on the CPU because
the model doesn't fit.

- **Type:** `unsigned integer, meaning >=0`
- **Default:** `99`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.apiKeyFile`

Runtime credential file on the serving host; never its contents.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.apiKeyFormat`

Credential file encoding.

- **Type:** `one of "env", "raw"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.baseUrl`

OpenAI API base URL on the serving host.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1"`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.cacheDirectory`

Persistent GGUF cache directory on the serving host.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.models`

Configured routing names, including idle models.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.platform`

Where operator commands run.

- **Type:** `one of "linux", "darwin"`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.port`

Loopback API port on the serving host.

- **Type:** `16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `8080`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/operator.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.port`

TCP port llama-server listens on. Also the port a Caddy route
(local or cross-host) reverse-proxies to.

Only the router binds this. Each loaded model gets its own
child process on an ephemeral loopback port, which the router
proxies to — those are not reachable from off-host, and they
inherit `LLAMA_API_KEY` from the router's environment, so they
are not an unauthenticated side door either.

- **Type:** `16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `8080`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.sleepIdleSeconds`

Idle seconds after which a loaded model sleeps and hands its
VRAM back (`--sleep-idle-seconds`). The point on a machine
that is also used for something else (a workstation that
games, a server that transcodes); the next request pays a
reload.

Passed to the router, which is inherited by every child, so it
is uniform across a host's models by construction. It is a
separate mechanism from `--models-max` eviction and both
apply: a sleeping model still counts as loaded, so asking for
a different model unloads the sleeper outright rather than
waiting for it to wake.

- **Type:** `positive integer, meaning >0`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Example:** `600`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix`](../../modules/system/_llama-cpp/common.nix)

### `myLlmMetrics.endpoints`

llama-server routers this host should publish metrics for,
keyed by the name that lands in the `llama_server` label.
Contributed by the route modules that already know an
endpoint exists — `llm.nix` for this host's own router,
the route module for a remote router.

Reachability is the only requirement: nothing here has to
run locally, and an endpoint that is down publishes
`llama_server_up 0` rather than failing the run.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/llm-metrics.nix`](../../modules/apps/llm-metrics.nix)

### `myLlmMetrics.endpoints.<name>.host`

Host the llama-server router listens on, as this host reaches it.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/llm-metrics.nix`](../../modules/apps/llm-metrics.nix)

### `myLlmMetrics.endpoints.<name>.port`

Port the llama-server router listens on.

- **Type:** `16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/llm-metrics.nix`](../../modules/apps/llm-metrics.nix)

## Messaging

MQTT broker users and ACLs.

### `myMosquitto.users`

Mosquitto users contributed by app modules. Each entry
provisions a sops secret for the user's password and renders
a username/ACL pair onto the single shared listener.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/mosquitto.nix`](../../modules/system/mosquitto.nix)

### `myMosquitto.users.<name>.acl`

Mosquitto ACL strings for this user (e.g.
`"readwrite hoymiles/#"`). Empty list grants the
user no topics — equivalent to disabling them.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "readwrite hoymiles/#"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/mosquitto.nix`](../../modules/system/mosquitto.nix)

### `myMosquitto.users.<name>.secretName`

sops secret name for this user's password.
Defaults to "&lt;name&gt;/mqtt_password".

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›/mqtt_password"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/mosquitto.nix`](../../modules/system/mosquitto.nix)

### `myMosquitto.users.<name>.username`

MQTT username. Defaults to the attribute name.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"‹name›"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/mosquitto.nix`](../../modules/system/mosquitto.nix)

## App-owned options

Options an individual app exposes for host wiring.

### `myBambuddy.virtualPrinter.address`

The DHCP-reserved vlan30 address the VP binds (reserved against
`mac` on the router). bambuddy requires a dedicated, stable IP
per VP for all services (MQTT/FTP/SSDP/Bind); this is the single
source for it — set the VP Bind IP and the slicer's printer IP
to this. Required when `enable` is set.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/bambuddy.nix`](../../modules/apps/bambuddy.nix)

### `myBambuddy.virtualPrinter.enable`

Whether to enable bambuddy's Virtual Printer macvlan on vlan30.

The VP (Proxy Mode) relays a slicer's print to a real Bambu
printer and needs a dedicated, STATIC vlan30 address for all its
services (MQTT/FTP/SSDP/Bind). Enabling this creates the
`iot-static` macvlan on the host's vlan30 parent and attaches the
bambuddy container to it at `address`, with `mac` pinned. Set it
from the host module (the address/MAC are a per-host DHCP
reservation), not from hostSpec — the VLAN parent stays generic
infrastructure (hostSpec.iotTrunkInterface), the VP identity is
this app's. Requires hostSpec.iotTrunkInterface to be set
.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/bambuddy.nix`](../../modules/apps/bambuddy.nix)

### `myBambuddy.virtualPrinter.mac`

Pinned MAC for the VP's macvlan leg on vlan30. podman assigns a
fresh random MAC on every container re-creation, which re-rolls
the DHCP lease and drifts the VP's IP — breaking the proxy's
bind and the slicer's by-IP device entry. Pinning the MAC
(paired with a DHCP reservation matching `address`) keeps the
dedicated address stable, which bambuddy requires. Required when
`enable` is set.

- **Type:** `null or string`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/bambuddy.nix`](../../modules/apps/bambuddy.nix)

### `myOmnigent.enable`

Whether to enable the Omnigent server. Off by default; see the header of
modules/apps/omnigent.nix for what turning it on does.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/omnigent.nix`](../../modules/apps/omnigent.nix)

### `myValheim.availablePlugins`

Pinned BepInEx plugin packages for `bepinexPlugins`. Each is
overridable: `.override { settings = { <section>.<key> = …; }; }`
renders that plugin's BepInEx config. Published as an option
so a host can select from it and so `task hashes` can reach
each `src` by flake attribute.

- **Type:** `attribute set of package`
- **Default:** the pinned packages in `_valheim/bepinex-plugins.nix`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.bepinex`

Have the image install BepInEx (the framework, from its own
Thunderstore lookup) and load plugins from /config/bepinex on
next container start. Required by `bepinexPlugins`; on its
own it also allows unmanaged local exploration by dropping a
DLL straight into
/var/lib/containers/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/. See the
"Mods" section at the top of this file, including why a mod
that works on dev is not thereby cleared for prod's player
load.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.bepinexPlugins`

Nix-built plugin trees installed into the container before it
starts — the reviewable alternative to hand-dropped DLLs.
Each package uses the layout documented in
`_valheim/bepinex-plugins.nix`; `availablePlugins` holds the
pinned ones. Removing an entry removes its files and its
declared config on the next start, and nothing outside the
managed subtree is touched (see
`_valheim/bepinex-materialize.sh` for exactly what is owned).

Requires `bepinex`. At most one networking plugin
(BetterNetworking10, FiresGhettoNetworking) at a time — both
patch ZDO send pacing, and a combined result would say
nothing about either.

- **Type:** `list of package`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    (config.myValheim.availablePlugins.betterNetworking10.override {
      settings."02 - Networking"."Queue Size" = "KB64";
    })
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.crossplay`

Run on Microsoft's PlayFab Party relay (`CROSSPLAY=true`)
instead of the Steam backend. See "Crossplay" and "Endpoint
exclusivity" at the top of this file for the full tradeoff.

Selects the backend only — the firewall rule and the join-code
notifier/watchdog follow it, the game port does not. Two hosts
behind one NAT are kept apart by `gamePort`, whichever backend
each runs.

`true` gets non-Steam clients (console, Microsoft Store) and
needs no inbound port-forward, at the cost of losing
connect-by-address entirely. `false` opens the game UDP ports
on the host firewall and players join by typing
`<host-lan-ip>:<gamePort>`, Steam clients only. Defaults to
`false`, the image's own default.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.enable`

Whether to enable the Valheim dedicated server container.

Gated on an option rather than on the import site because this
module ships via `commonApps` in ../profiles/server-apps.nix,
which also covers tests-server — and making the quarterly
recovery-drill VM download 1.5 GB of steamcmd and run a game
server is pure cost. The two real servers opt in from their host
files, which also puts "does this host run Valheim, and with
crossplay?" in one place instead of split across the profile and
a host module.
.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.gamePort`

UDP game port (`SERVER_PORT`). The query port is always this
+ 1 — the image derives `SERVER_QUERY_PORT=$((SERVER_PORT + 1))`
and offers no separate knob. 2456 is the image's default.

**Every concurrently running Valheim host behind the same
public IP needs a distinct value, regardless of `crossplay`.**
What a PlayFab lobby advertises is `<public-ip>:<gamePort>`,
a join code resolves to that endpoint, and a Steam-backend
server registers a lobby too — so two hosts on one port
answer each other's codes (2026-09-11 with both on crossplay,
2026-09-21 with one on Steam). This module cannot check that
across separate host evaluations; the host files carry the
assignments side by side for that reason. See "Endpoint
exclusivity" at the top of this file.

- **Type:** `16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)`
- **Default:** `2456`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.joincodeWebhookSecret`

Key in this host's sops file holding the Discord webhook that
valheim-joincode-notify and valheim-joincode-watchdog post to.
Only read when `crossplay` is set.

A key name rather than a toggle so that a second crossplay
host can keep its join codes out of the players' channel
without losing the notifier: the watchdog's re-registration
loop refuses to run unless the notifier is active, so dropping
the unit would take detection and recovery with it. Point this
at a dev-only channel by naming a key here and setting it in
that host's sops file (`task secrets:edit:<host>`; a Discord
webhook URL is pasted in, not generated, so this is not a
`task secrets:secret` case).

A key another module also declares (e.g. alertmanager's
`discord/alerts_webhook`) is fine — sops-nix merges the two
declarations and each module's `restartUnits` accumulate.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"valheim/discord_webhook"`
- **Example:** `"discord/alerts_webhook"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.playerNotify`

Post player join/leave to the `valheim/player_webhook`
Discord channel.

Unlike `valheim-joincode-notify`, this is a channel-noise
choice and not a backend requirement — the journal lines it
keys off (`Got character ZDOID`, `Destroying abandoned non
persistent zdo`) are emitted identically on the Steam
backend. Turned off on the dev instance because the audience
for a mod-test server is whoever is at the terminal, and its
join/leave traffic in the players' channel is noise. If dev
traffic is ever wanted, point `valheim/player_webhook` in
that host's sops file at a different channel
(`task secrets:edit:<host>`) and flip this back on.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.serverArgs`

Extra valheim_server argv tokens, appended after the ones the
image builds itself and after `worldModifiers`. Rendered,
together with `worldModifiers`, as the image's `SERVER_ARGS`
only when nonempty, so a host that sets nothing keeps an
unchanged unit (an empty `SERVER_ARGS` would still rewrite it
and restart the server, rotating the join code).

One list element is one argv token. The image expands
`$SERVER_ARGS` unquoted, so a token holding whitespace or a
glob character would be split or expanded; an assertion
rejects those instead of letting the argv differ from the
declaration. It also rejects the flags the image already
passes (`-name`, `-port`, `-world`, `-public`, `-password`,
`-crossplay`, …) and the world modifier flags (`-preset`,
`-modifier`, `-setkey`, `-resetmodifiers`) — those have
typed options or come from the module, and a second copy
would leave which one wins up to the game's parser.

Only for arguments the server binary is verified to accept;
see "Mods and dev experiments" in `_valheim/README.md`.

- **Type:** `list of string`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "-saveinterval"
    "900"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.combat`

`-modifier Combat <value>`, applied after
`preset`.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `null or one of "veryeasy", "easy", "hard", "veryhard"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.deathPenalty`

`-modifier DeathPenalty <value>`, applied after
`preset`.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `null or one of "casual", "veryeasy", "easy", "hard", "hardcore"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.portals`

`-modifier Portals <value>`, applied after
`preset`.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `null or one of "casual", "hard", "veryhard"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.preset`

World difficulty preset (`-preset`). Clears every other
world modifier before applying its own, so the module
renders it ahead of the `-modifier`/`-setkey` tokens and
those refine it.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `null or one of "normal", "casual", "easy", "hard", "hardcore", "immersive", "hammer"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Example:** `"hard"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.raids`

`-modifier Raids <value>`, applied after
`preset`.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `null or one of "none", "muchless", "less", "more", "muchmore"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.resources`

`-modifier Resources <value>`, applied after
`preset`. This is the drop-rate knob.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `null or one of "muchless", "less", "more", "muchmore", "most"`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

### `myValheim.worldModifiers.setKeys`

Checkbox world modifiers, one `-setkey <key>` each. The
game adds any string here as a world key without a log
line or an error, so this list is the only check.

Saved into the world (its starting keys, in the world
metadata file), so unsetting this does not undo it on its
own. With `preset`
set the next start re-applies the whole declaration, since
a preset clears every modifier first; without one, roll
back with a single start on `preset = "normal"`, then
unset that too.

- **Type:** `list of (one of "nobuildcost", "playerevents", "passivemobs", "nomap")`
- **Default:** `[ ]`
- **Example:**

  ```nix
  [
    "nomap"
  ]
  ```
- **Declared in:** [`modules/apps/valheim.nix`](../../modules/apps/valheim.nix)

## Coding agents (home-manager)

Home-manager options, set under a user's `home-manager.users.<name>` (or a standalone home configuration); evaluated here in a stub home-manager configuration with only the `vibes` module (`modules/programs/pi.nix`, `modules/programs/vibes.nix`).

### `myPi.enable`

Whether to enable the pi coding agent.

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `true`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.package`

pi package, shared by Linux and Darwin configurations.

- **Type:** `package`
- **Default:** _computed from other options; see the declaration_
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.providers`

Additive provider declarations rendered into one models.json. Work-only providers belong in the private work module.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (open submodule of (JSON value))`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.providers.<name>.api`

pi API dialect, such as openai-responses or anthropic-messages.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"openai-completions"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.providers.<name>.apiKey`

Runtime credential reference, for example !command or $ENV_VAR; never a secret value.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.providers.<name>.baseUrl`

API base URL, before pi adds its API-specific path.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.providers.<name>.models`

Models advertised by this provider, with optional pi metadata.

- **Type:** `list of (open submodule of (JSON value))`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myPi.providers.<name>.models.*.id`

Model identifier sent to this provider.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/pi.nix`](../../modules/programs/pi.nix)

### `myVibes.agentPackages`

The coding-agent CLIs this aspect installs, keyed by name.

- **Type:** `attribute set of package`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/programs/vibes.nix`](../../modules/programs/vibes.nix)

## Local LLM inference (nix-darwin)

Options the nix-darwin side of `myLlamaCpp` adds to the shared ones above (`modules/system/_llama-cpp/darwin.nix`, registered by `modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`); evaluated here in a stub `aarch64-darwin` system with only that module.

### `myLlamaCpp.dataDirectory`

User-owned persistent model data and local API credential; outside the Nix store.

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"/Users/fixture/Library/Application Support/llama-cpp"`
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.operator.prunePackage`

Darwin prune executable with the same algorithm and GNU runtime as Linux.

- **Type:** `package`
- **Default:** none (required)
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)

### `myLlamaCpp.piProvider`

Published pi provider metadata for the local router; contains a runtime key-file reference.

- **Type:** `attribute set of (JSON value)`
- **Default:** `{ }`
- **Read-only:** set by the declaring module
- **Declared in:** [`modules/system/llama-cpp.nix`](../../modules/system/llama-cpp.nix)
